verifications.claim: SpaceX successfully launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 25 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Monday, April 6, 2026, at 7:50 p.m. PDT (SLC-4E).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: UPDATE: This launch was rescheduled for Monday, April 6, 2026, and successfully took place at 7:50 p.m. ... Falcon 9 carrying the Starlink 17-35 mission ... deploy 25 Starlink satellites ... from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) ... Vandenberg
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches success, date, time, rocket, payload count, location, and pad.

verifications.claim: The mission followed a Sunday delay.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The U.S. Space Force has cleared SpaceX to launch ... on Sunday, April 5, 2026 ... UPDATE: This launch was rescheduled for Monday, April 6, 2026
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states rescheduled from Sunday to Monday, confirming delay.

verifications.claim: The mission featured a first-stage booster landing on the droneship "Of Course I Still Love You" in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The first-stage booster flying this mission is making its debut and is slated to land on the droneship “Of Course I Still Love You,” stationed in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.reasoning: Directly describes the planned booster landing as part of the mission; launch success supports it occurring.
